doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Parents, siblings and the extended Cuban family
summary: Names, origins and ages of his parents, his brother and sister, and the large family on his mother's side.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And what were your parents’ names?
My father’s name was Paquito Francisco, and my mother was Maura Figuerez.
Where are your parents from?
My mother is from the Riento Province, the city of Santiago de Cuba. My father is from Havana.
How old were your parents when you were born?
My father was 36, and my mother was 25.
Do you have other brothers and sisters?
I have a brother, Enrique which was born in 1950, and Rosario, which was born in 1961.
Where did you spend the majority of your childhood?
Uh, in my neighborhood, in Marinao.
So, you pretty much lived in that particular neighborhood for all of your years growing up?
All my life, I live there until I, I mean yea, in the same neighborhood, until I came to Spain first, and then six months later to New York, yes.
Do you come from a large family?
On my mother’s side yes; it’s a large family. My father was the littlest born.
Where was the majority of your family from?
All of them Cubans. My mother’s father was from Santiago; my father’s father from Havana. So, they were supposed to hate each other, but no, they love each other. [Both laugh]
Did your parents have brothers and sisters?
My mother had eight brothers and sisters. My father was, uh, just him.
He was an only child?
The only child.
